title: AST SAR: Kotzebue [AK26007932]
summary: On January 26, 2025, at 7:45 pm, Alaska State Troopers received a report of a search and rescue in the Kotzebue area. It was reported that Clifford Melton, age 61, of Kotzebue, had left Kotzebue on a snowmachine earlier that day, heading to Buckland, and hadn't been heard from since. Ground crews from Buckland and Kotzebue searched the trail. On January 27, 2026, troopers were able to land an AWT aircraft on skis near an abandoned cabin approximately 35 miles south of Kotzebue and located Melton in the cabin, extremely hypothermic. Ground crews arrived and helped load him on the plane, where he was transported to Kotzebue and then medevac'd to an Anchorage area hospital, where he died as a result of his injuries. Next of kin have been notified.

Investigation determined Jeffery Harris, age 42 of Anchorage, took the moose on the evening of September 5th. The moose was left in the field for approximately 14 hours before being field dressed. Temperatures throughout the region were warm and wet. The meat of the moose spoiled due to not being properly cared for in a timely manner. Investigation also determined Harris took the two front shoulders, and other chunks of meat, and discarded them in the brush due to their putrid smell and colors. Harris was issued a citation for failing to salvage all edible meat. The moose rack and rotten meat were seized as evidence. Arraignment was set for October 9, 2025, in the Aniak Court.
sourceAttribution: Source: Alaska State Troopers Daily Dispatch

title: AST Death Investigation: Anchorage [AK25067686]
summary: On July 11, 2025, at around 1:00 am, a fight occurred in a cell between two inmates at the Anchorage Correctional Center. Correctional Officers responded to the fight, and 53-year-old inmate Jeffrey Foreman became combative and charged officers who were giving commands to Foreman. Officers used force to put Foreman on the ground and began restraining him. While being restrained, Foreman kicked an officer and was placed in leg restraints. Shortly after he was restrained, Foreman became unresponsive, and lifesaving efforts were started immediately by correctional staff and later the Anchorage Fire Department. Despite these efforts, Foreman was declared deceased at the facility. His next of kin have been notified, and his body has been sent to the State Medical Examiner’s Office for autopsy.

summary: This week, the Alaska State Troopers and Fairbanks Police Department arrested Gareth Ward for allegedly sexually assaulting multiple juveniles in the Fairbanks area. title: AST SAR: Tuntutuliak [AK25063257]
summary: On June 30, 2025, Alaska State Troopers received an SOS activation reporting a boat with multiple people aboard ran aground on a sand bar on the Kuskokwim River near Tuntutuliak. summary: Alaska State Troopers, in coordination with the Alaska Mountain Rescue Group (AMRG), successfully rescued a hiker in distress near the Indian Creek Trailhead late Saturday night. At approximately 11:22 PM on April 19, authorities received an SOS activation from a Garmin device belonging to a 52-year-old male hiking alone in the Indian Creek area. The hiker, who had undergone knee replacement surgery last October, was reported overdue by a companion waiting at the trailhead. The rescue operation proceeded despite a brief cancellation of the SOS call, as the hiker later reported he couldn't feel his feet. After midnight, the Alaska Mountain Rescue Group was deployed to the last known coordinates. At approximately 2:55 AM, rescuers made contact with the hiker about a mile from the parking lot

summary: On 4/27/20, Alaska Wildlife Troopers on Prince of Wales Island were notified of several deer that had been taken illegally during the closed season. The deer appeared to have been recently killed (within the past 12 hours). Several items of evidence were located at the scene, and the investigation is ongoing. title: AST Snowmachine/Musher collision: Galena [AK20015147]
summary: Update: The driver of snowmachine contacted AST and is cooperating with the ongoing investigation. Original Text: On 3/2/2020, Alaska State Troopers in Galena received a report that a musher who was participating in the Serum Run was struck the night prior, at approximately 2030 hours, by a snowmachiner about five miles outside of Galena. Investigation revealed that Kirsten Bey, 64 of Nome, was mushing to Galena from Ruby when she was struck by an unknown snowmachiner. Another participant, riding snowmachine, came upon the scene shortly after and helped transport Bey to Galena. The snowmachiner that hit the musher remained on scene until Bey was transported away. Bey was medivaced from Galena to the Fairbanks Medical Hospital with significant injuries. The incident is under investigation.
